'''T. Edward "Ed" Damer''' (August 16, 1937 - March 21, 2024) was an American philosopher, author, father, and grandfather.

==Biography==
Damer was a professor of philosophy and chair of the Division Visual and Performing Arts at [[Emory and Henry College]] in [[Emory, Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= http://www.ehc.edu/directories/faculty.html#d|title= Faculty Directory - D|publisher= [[Emory and Henry College]]|accessdate= 2009-01-22}}</ref> He started on the Emory faculty in 1967 and retired in 2012.<ref>[http://www.ehc.edu/t-edward-damer Faculty biography], retrieved 2011-04-27.</ref> In 1991, he won the James A. David Faculty Recognition Award from the Emory alumni in recognition of his teaching.<ref>{{citation|title=Veteran Professor Recognized|date=May 29, 1991|journal=[[Roanoke Times]]}}.</ref>

==Works==
He is the author of ''[[Attacking Faulty Reasoning]]'', a textbook on logical [[fallacies]]. The book defines and explains 60 of the most commonly committed fallacies. It also gives specific suggestions about how to address or to "attack" each fallacy when it is encountered.<ref name=Damer2009>{{citation |year=2009 |author=Damer, T. Edward |title=Attacking Faulty Reasoning: A Practical Guide to Fallacy-free Arguments |edition=6th |place=Belmont, California |publisher=Wadsworth |isbn=978-0-495-09506-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-qZabUx0FmkC&q=faulty+reasoning |accessdate=30 November 2010}}</ref> The organization of the fallacies comes from the author's own theories that have accumulated through years of research and study, which defines a fallacy as a violation of one of the five criteria of a good argument.
